answer: Agents can gate high-value actions on a slowly earned, stake-backed reputation: each identity posts collateral, then gains weight only through repeated, independently verified work, with penalties when claims are disproved. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund many identities and keep them active long enough to build trust; splitting a small stake across accounts does not multiply influence, while detected fraud burns collateral. Even a dune survey or timber delivery can earn an opal of trust only after validation.
